topIssues.title: C-flake: TestUnsafeChainNotStalling_ELSync (Short, Long, RestartOpNode)
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Tracking flaky test investigation.

**Test:** `TestUnsafeChainNotStalling_ELSync_Short`, `TestUnsafeChainNotStalling_ELSync_Long`, `TestUnsafeChainNotStalling_ELSync_RestartOpNode_Long`
**Package:** `github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-acceptance-tests/tests/depreqres/syncmodereqressync/elsync`
**Job:** `memory-all` (flake-shake gate)
**Flakes:** 1 each in recent CI data

All three tests share the same `UnsafeChainNotStalling_Disconnect` / `UnsafeChainNotStalling_RestartOpNode` helpers. The helpers use `time.Sleep` for disconnect duration and P2P disconnect/reconnect patterns that may be timing-sensitive under CI load. The `stableSyncStatus` helper polls for head stabilization but uses a 5-second timeout that may be insufficient.

topIssues.title: ZKDisputeGame: Handle address(0) bond credit claiming via monitoring or contract change
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
## Context

In `ZKDisputeGame`, when a parent game resolves as `CHALLENGER_WINS` and the child was never challenged, `claimData.challenger` is `address(0)`. The `resolve()` function assigns `totalBonds` to `normalModeCredit[address(0)]` — the bond is effectively "burned" by crediting the zero address.

However, nobody will call `claimCredit(address(0))` to actually move the funds through the DelayedWETH two-phase withdrawal, so the ETH remains stranded in DelayedWETH indefinitely.

This was identified during review of ethereum-optimism/optimism#19606:
https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19606#discussion_r2972200379

## Options Discussed

1. **Monitoring approach (current plan):** Update monitoring to account for the fact that `address(0)` credits will never be claimed, so they don't show up as anomalies. The ETH stays in DelayedWETH — monitoring just needs to understand this is expected.

2. **Contract-level approach:** Piggyback on other `claimCredit()` calls to automatically process `address(0)` credit at the same time. Downside: makes the code messier.

3. **Automatic burn in `resolve()`:** Not feasible due to DelayedWETH's two-phase withdrawal — both phases can't happen in a single transaction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide on approach (monitoring adjustment vs contract change)
- [ ] If monitoring: update `dispute-mon` to expect that `address(0)` credit in ZK games is never claimed, so it doesn't flag as an anomaly
- [ ] If contract: implement and test the piggyback approach in `ZKDisputeGame`
- [ ] Ensure monitoring correctly accounts for ETH held in DelayedWETH from ZK game bond burns

## Related

- ethereum-optimism/optimism#18424 — broader ZK game monitoring issue
- ethereum-optimism/optimism#19606 — ZKDisputeGame implementation PR where this was identified

topPRs.title: test(kona-proof-interop): add multi-iteration EIP-2935 test
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #19726. Adds a test for the multi-iteration EIP-2935 lookup case where the target block is beyond the 8,191-block history window, as requested in [review](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19726#discussion_r2113282170).

- **New test**: `test_header_by_number_eip2935_multi_iteration` — target is 8,196 blocks behind safe head, requiring two EIP-2935 lookups through an intermediate block
- **Unified fixture format**: Both single and multi-iteration tests now share one `FixtureData` struct with a `steps: Vec<ProofStep>` array. Each step holds account/storage proof nodes and the resolved block header. Eliminates duplicate structs and loaders.

### How the multi-iteration lookup works

1. **Iteration 1**: Target outside window (N-M=8,196 > 8,191) → reads slot `N % 8191` from safe head's state → returns hash of oldest block in window (intermediate)
2. **Iteration 2**: Target inside window (I-M=5 ≤ 8,191) → reads slot `M % 8191` from intermediate block's state → returns actual target hash

Fixture contains two sets of `eth_getProof` data (at safe head and at intermediate block) plus three block headers.

Refs: #18288

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo nextest run --package kona-proof-interop` — all 28 tests pass
- [x] `cargo clippy -p kona-proof-interop --all-targets --all-features` — no warnings
- [x] No production code modified
